### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/rest`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s).

**33** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **34** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `638bed803cfdf4c818bfb36dc0da77f63cf26f03` — the merge of head `76b0bde682ce7e0c1b775687c86b0bd40eb125cd` into base `6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 638bed803cfdf4c818bfb36dc0da77f63cf26f03 && git checkout 638bed803cfdf4c818bfb36dc0da77f63cf26f03
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3 76b0bde682ce7e0c1b775687c86b0bd40eb125cd && git checkout -B drift-repro 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3 && git merge --no-ff 76b0bde682ce7e0c1b775687c86b0bd40eb125cd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6538ba48fc4590402cd6280cf83a8902f6de83d3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The store-violation path asks the refusal's question.** `writeBack` swaps `uniqueViolationColumn` for `uniqueViolationField` (`@objectstack/types`, landed with #32935), which sets aside the implied `organization_id` key part. So a `unique: 'organization'` field's `(organization_id, FIELD)` violation now names FIELD. Pinned for both spellings: SQLite `UNIQUE constraint failed: invoice.organization_id, invoice.invoice_no` and Postgres `23505` with `Key (organization_id, invoice_no)=…`. The card's control is pinned too: a key of two authored columns (`series, invoice_no`) still names no field.
- **One label resolution.** `fieldLabelOf` calls the engine envelope's own `displayLabels` (`duplicate-record-error.ts`) with the restorer's `validationMessageContext`, which `engine.ts` now hands the restore host the same way the other hosts get it. Both unique refusals therefore read one label: translation, else declared `label`, else absent (pinned: no label means no `fieldLabel`, and the API name is never repeated there). Both the probe before the write and the store's violation at it use it (the PR body says the dev chose this so one code names its field one way), and both are pinned, the translated locale included.
- `message` uses the label and `developerMessage` keeps the API name. `field` stays the API name. The REST door adds `fieldLabel` to `REFUSAL_DETAIL_KEYS`, pinned in `recycle-bin-routes.test.ts`.
- `writeBack` is called with `.call(this, …)` (restore.ts:451), so `fieldLabelOf.call(this, …)` inside it has the host.
- CI on this head: 36 success, 20 skipped, none failed. `mergeable_state: clean`.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/rest` patch, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`: right. `displayLabels` becomes a module export of `duplicate-record-error.ts`, but the package root re-exports only `DuplicateRecordError` and `DUPLICATE_RECORD_CODE` from that module, so no public export moves.

### ③ Boundary flags

- None. No authorization or tenancy read changes, and the label is the caller-locale display text the engine envelope already serves.
- Nit N1: the `id` case (a live row holds the entry's id) also carries `fieldLabel` (the `id` field's label) in `details`, while its message stays the id sentence. That is harmless and consistent with `field: 'id'`. Leaving it out would be the tidier spelling.
